question: In the release screen the old page write answered 200 and changed no row on the first of three writes on 15.3.0, 16.5.0 and 16.6.0 (and once on 14.6.0 in the morning's probe). Is that a fault of the frozen write step, and can it happen on 14.0.0, which Stage A uses?
cases: the public example family on disposable records; the frozen three-arm/write-step.mjs unchanged

rounds.what: one write per fresh sign-in on a warm instance, the dialog's field and the request logged
rounds.seen: the field held the hours typed before Save; the form check was sent, then one save carrying the hours typed; the row changed within about 0.3 s

rounds.what: the frozen executeWorkWrite itself on a warm instance, a new browser per write
the frozen executeWorkWrite as the first page action after the release's container was restarted and had answered five API calls in a row; every request and answer on the work package timed

findings: UPDATE after round 5: with the hardened step, 100 of 100 first writes after a cold start on 14.0.0 landed with the hours asked, and no save went out before the dialog's form check was answered.

UPDATE after round 4: the fault does happen on 14.0.0. In the 10th of the further cold-start writes the field ended up holding 856 and the server stored 856 hours. The statement below that 14.0.0 showed no anomaly was true of the first 20 only.

On 14.0.0, the release Stage A decides routes on: no anomaly in 20 writes made as the first action after a cold start, which is the condition that matters, since every anomaly seen came right after the application started and each arm's unseen-route phase starts that way. The 50 clean warm writes on 14.0.0 do not bear on it.

On 16.6.0 after a cold start: 2 anomalies in 20. In one, the save was sent with the right hours while the form check was still unanswered, both were answered 200, and the row never changed. In the other, the hours typed were joined to the text the dialog already showed (8h and 56 became 8h56) and the row was changed to 8.93 hours: a write with the wrong value.

'First write of a browser session' is not the trigger: 0 anomalies in 100 such writes on warm instances. All anomalies seen so far, here and in the screen, were on releases later than 14.0.0 and came right after the application had started.

On those later releases the dialog formats the field as text (8h) and reacts while it is being filled. The frozen write step was recorded for 14.0.0 and does not wait for that. A second upgrade to such a release needs a write step made for it, with the field checked before Save and the stored value checked after, as part of that stage's own freeze.
whatThisDoesNotShow: that the fault cannot happen on 14.0.0. 0 of 20 cold-start writes bounds the rate below 13.9 percent (one-sided 95 percent), which is too weak. An earlier version of this receipt quoted 4.2 percent from 0 of 70; that mixed in warm writes, which are not the triggering condition. Corrected at the evaluator's review.
releaseScreenUnaffected: check 1 needs the old write to commit in 0 of 3; 2 of 3 is still not met, so no screening result changes.

round4.what: 80 more first writes after a cold start on 14.0.0 through the frozen executeWorkWrite, to make 100 in all

expectedWrittenBeforeAnyResult.anomalies: 0 of 80: every write lands with the hours asked
expectedWrittenBeforeAnyResult.ifAnyAnomaly: the write step is hardened and the runner re-frozen before Stage A
expectedWrittenBeforeAnyResult.ifNone: 0 of 100 bounds the rate below about 3 percent (one-sided 95 percent); the frozen step stays
expectedWrittenBeforeAnyResult.clockNote: An earlier version said 17:55:00Z, a time typed by hand that was ahead of the commit that carried it (722c2fbbd, 17:47 UTC). The commit time is the record.

anomaly.what: the hours typed were joined to the value the field already held (8 and 56 became 856) and the server stored 856 hours: a write with the wrong value, on the release Stage A uses

results.againstExpectation: MISS: expected 0 of 80; 1 anomaly at the 10th write. On 14.0.0, first writes after a cold start now stand at 1 anomaly in 31.
results.consequence: as ruled beforehand: the write step is hardened and the runner re-frozen before Stage A

clockNote: Times typed into receipts by hand on 2026-11-23 were approximate. Where a time and its commit disagree, the commit time is the record.

round5.what: the hardened write step (waits for the form check's answer, reads the field back, does not press Save unless it holds exactly the hours asked), 100 first writes after a cold start on 14.0.0

expectedWrittenBeforeAnyResult.anomalies: 0 of 100: every write lands with the hours asked, or, if the field cannot be made to hold them, Save is not pressed and the record says so (counted separately as 'not attempted', expected 0)
expectedWrittenBeforeAnyResult.ifAnyWrongValueOrUnchangedRow: the hardening is not good enough; it is reworked before any freeze

ranOn.note: commits made while it ran touched only the Stage A notes; no file the run reads changed

results.againstExpectation: as expected: 0 anomalies of 100, Save not pressed 0 of 100
results.bound: 0 of 100 bounds the rate of an anomaly below about 3 percent (one-sided 95 percent). It does not prove zero.

runsOn.note: the hardened step as committed; a first start of this round on uncommitted bytes was stopped after 2 clean writes at the evaluator's request and is not counted
